summary_paragraph: A woman with a complex medical history including type 1 diabetes, pancreas and multiple kidney transplants, end-stage renal disease on peritoneal dialysis, and heart disease was admitted from rehabilitation with fever and hypotension. She was diagnosed with E. coli bacteremia and septic shock. She was initially managed in the ICU with fluids, stress-dose steroids, and broad-spectrum antibiotics, later narrowed to meropenem. The source of bacteremia remained unclear despite evaluation including CT and echocardiogram. She improved clinically with resolution of fever and stabilization of blood pressure, and was transitioned to oral medications and a midline for outpatient IV antibiotics. Her anemia improved with continued Epogen, hypothyroidism was addressed with increased levothyroxine, and her transplant and cardiac regimens were maintained. She was discharged to extended care with plans for infectious disease and nephrology follow-up.
